_: Wed 7 Oct 2026 · teaching slot. Primary source READ on 2 Oct 2026: In re UPL Advisory Opinion 2003-2, 277 Ga. 472 (2003), State Bar of Georgia PDF. Quote: 'we have consistently held that it is the unauthorized practice of law for someone other than a duly-licensed Georgia attorney to close a real estate transaction or to prepare or facilitate the execution of such deed(s) for the benefit of a seller, borrower, or lender.' Statute O.C.G.A. 15-19-50 lists conveyancing and title opinions as practicing law (FindLaw text). The card says an attorney closes the sale and never names a price, fee or which attorney.
headline:
In Georgia, An Attorney
Closes Your Home Sale
turn_1: Echo, in Georgia only a licensed Georgia attorney can close a home sale. The Georgia Supreme Court confirmed it in 2003.
turn_2: Not my agent? I thought my agent took care of the whole thing.
turn_3: Your agent guides the sale. The attorney handles the legal side of the closing, including the deed. Two different jobs.
echo_line: So the agent guides it and the attorney closes it. Two jobs. I'd want that clear before closing day.
source: In re UPL Advisory Opinion 2003-2, 277 Ga. 472 (2003) · retrieved Oct 2, 2026
disclaimer: General information about Georgia practice, not legal advice. Ask a Georgia real estate attorney about your own closing.
